THIS ONE IS LIKE A BABY WRAPPED UP IN A TAGUA NUT. So, in this case, you can see what a tagua nut looks like, because the baby is carved into the side of it, and the rest of it remains. I assume it's polished up pretty well. (It does not come with the wooden display stand.) The Tagua nuts were harvested in Zambia (Africa) and then sent to China for carving. The Tagua tree is a palm tree that grows freely in some subtropical climates, but is absolutely not grown in China. The Tagua nut is very hard and takes on a beautiful ivory or darker than ivory, amber color. For this reason, Tagua is sometimes known as Vegetable Ivory. The composition of the Tagua nut is so similar to mammal tusk that it is difficult for some people to tell them apart. For me, I feel like I can easily tell them apart. The carved tagua nuts I'm selling here are wonderful, but I don't think they look like they are creme-color, or light enough to be mistaken for ivory. Perhaps they have turned to amber over time?
